A) Extrinsic arterial compression	Extrinsic compression (tumor, lymph node) is rare and would typically present with other mass-related symptoms.
C) Mid-aortic syndrome	Mid-aortic syndrome = segmental narrowing of abdominal aorta. Very rare. Would cause upper > lower extremity BP differential.
D) Premature atherosclerosis	Atherosclerotic RAS occurs in OLDER patients (>50) with risk factors (smoking, DM, hyperlipidemia). A 21-year-old without risk factors → FMD, not atherosclerosis.
E) Spontaneous renal artery dissection	Very rare. Would present acutely with flank pain, not chronic HTN with LVH.
IF young woman + severe HTN + abdominal bruit → THEN fibromuscular dysplasia

✅ Correct Answer: D) <7500/mm³
🔑 KEY CONCEPT
🔑 In a normal (Gaussian) distribution, the mean divides the distribution exactly in half

🔑 50% of values fall BELOW the mean and 50% fall ABOVE the mean

🔑 Mean = 7500 → 50% have WBC <7500

🧠 MULTI-STEP LOGIC

[Step 1] Normal distribution is SYMMETRIC around the mean

[Step 2] Mean = median = mode in a normal distribution

[Step 3] 50% of values are BELOW the mean

50% of values are ABOVE the mean

[Step 4] 50% have WBC < 7500/mm³ ✓

❌ DISTRACTOR ANALYSIS
Choice	Why It's Wrong
A) 5500–9500/mm³	This is mean ± 2 SD = 95% of values. Not 50%.
B) 6500 or >8500/mm³	This is OUTSIDE mean ± 1 SD = ~32% of values (tails). Not 50%.
C) 6500–8500/mm³	This is mean ± 1 SD = ~68% of values. Not 50%.
E) >9500/mm³	This is above mean + 2 SD = ~2.5% of values. Not 50%.

sections.body:
🔑 Mucocutaneous bleeding (nosebleeds, bruising) = platelet disorder

🔑 Normal platelet count (300,000) = qualitative (functional) platelet defect

🔑 Normal ristocetin response = vWF and GPIb are NORMAL (ristocetin tests vWF-GPIb binding)

🔑 NO aggregation to thrombin = platelets cannot aggregate with each other

🔑 Normal PT and aPTT = coagulation cascade is intact

🔑 Family history (brother affected) = inherited disorder

🔑 Platelet aggregation failure with normal adhesion = Glanzmann thrombasthenia

🔑 Glanzmann = deficiency/dysfunction of GPIIb/IIIa (fibrinogen receptor on platelets)

🔑 GPIIb/IIIa binds fibrinogen → cross-links platelets → aggregation

🧠 MULTI-STEP LOGIC

[Step 1] Mucocutaneous bleeding + normal platelet count

→ Qualitative platelet disorder

[Step 2] Normal ristocetin → vWF and GPIb are fine

         → Rules out [vWD](/rare-disease/von-willebrand-disease) and Bernard-Soulier

[Step 3] No aggregation to thrombin → platelets can't

cross-link with each other

[Step 4] Aggregation requires GPIIb/IIIa + fibrinogen

[Step 5] Defect = GPIIb/IIIa ✓ (Glanzmann thrombasthenia)

❌ DISTRACTOR ANALYSIS
Choice	Why It's Wrong
A) Factor VII	Factor VII deficiency → prolonged PT. PT is NORMAL here. Also, factor deficiency → deep tissue bleeding, not mucocutaneous.
B) Fibrinogen	Fibrinogen deficiency → prolonged PT AND aPTT (fibrinogen is in the common pathway). Both are normal here.
D) Granule storage pool	Storage pool disease → decreased dense granule release → impaired aggregation to ADP/collagen. But aggregation to THROMBIN (a strong agonist) would still partially occur. Complete absence of aggregation → GPIIb/IIIa defect.
E) von Willebrand factor	vWF deficiency → abnormal RISTOCETIN test. Ristocetin response is NORMAL here. Rules out vWD.

36-year-old Icelandic woman… invasive ductal carcinoma… no family history… BRCA2 999del5 mutation… this mutation causes 9% of all breast cancers in Iceland. Best explanation for prevalence?

✅ Correct Answer: C) Geographically isolated population

sections.title: 🔑 HIGHLIGHTED VIGNETTE CLUES
sections.body:
🔑 Iceland = small, geographically isolated island population

🔑 Single specific mutation (999del5) accounts for 9% of ALL breast cancers in Iceland

🔑 This is an example of the founder effect — a specific mutation is highly prevalent in a population because the population descended from a small number of founders

🔑 Geographic isolation → limited gene flow → founder mutations persist at high frequency

❌ DISTRACTOR ANALYSIS
Choice	Why It's Wrong
A) Bottleneck reduction due to breast cancer	A bottleneck would REDUCE the population, but breast cancer doesn't cause mass population death. Also, bottleneck would reduce genetic diversity generally, not specifically increase one mutation.
B) Genetic heterogeneity	Genetic heterogeneity = DIFFERENT mutations causing the SAME disease. This is the OPPOSITE — ONE specific mutation is highly prevalent.
D) Heterozygote advantage	Heterozygote advantage (like sickle cell trait protecting against malaria) would require a survival benefit for carriers. No known survival advantage for BRCA2 carriers.
E) Random mating in a very large population	Iceland is a SMALL, isolated population — not large. Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in a large population would actually DILUTE rare mutations.

45-year-old woman… end-stage renal disease (IgA glomerulopathy)… kidney transplant… within 10 minutes of blood release, organ becomes swollen with multiple hemorrhages. Most likely cause?

✅ Correct Answer: D) Preformed antibodies in the recipient

sections.title: 🔑 HIGHLIGHTED VIGNETTE CLUES
sections.body:
🔑 Kidney transplant → immediate reaction

🔑 Within 10 minutes = HYPERACUTE rejection

🔑 Swollen + hemorrhagic = vascular thrombosis and necrosis

🔑 Hyperacute rejection = preformed antibodies in the RECIPIENT against donor antigens (ABO or HLA)

🔑 These antibodies bind donor endothelium → activate complement → thrombosis → graft destruction within minutes to hours

🧠 MULTI-STEP LOGIC

[Step 1] Transplant → blood released into kidney

[Step 2] Within MINUTES → swelling + hemorrhage

[Step 3] Timeframe = HYPERACUTE rejection

(minutes to hours)

[Step 4] Mechanism: PREFORMED ANTIBODIES in recipient ✓

→ bind donor vascular endothelium

→ complement activation

→ fibrinoid necrosis + thrombosis

[Step 5] Prevention: ABO matching + crossmatch testing

❌ DISTRACTOR ANALYSIS
Choice	Why It's Wrong
A) Perfusate hypersensitivity in donor	The donor kidney is no longer in the donor. Donor hypersensitivity is irrelevant.
B) Perfusate hypersensitivity in recipient	Perfusate reactions are rare and don't cause this classic hyperacute pattern.
C) Preformed antibodies in donor	Donor antibodies would be in the transplanted kidney's blood, but they are washed out during perfusion. The recipient's antibodies attack the graft.
E) Sensitized CD8+ T cells in donor	T-cell mediated rejection takes DAYS to WEEKS (acute rejection). Not minutes.
F) Sensitized CD8+ T cells in recipient	Same — T-cell mediated = acute rejection (days-weeks) or chronic rejection (months-years). Not hyperacute (minutes).

sections.title: 🔑 HIGHLIGHTED VIGNETTE CLUES
sections.body:
🔑 Bisphosphonate use (for multiple myeloma bone disease)

🔑 Midshaft femoral fracture with no trauma = atypical femoral fracture

🔑 Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclasts → suppress bone REMODELING

🔑 Excessive suppression of bone remodeling → bone becomes brittle (can't repair microdamage) → atypical fractures (subtrochanteric or midshaft femur)

🔑 This is a known complication of long-term bisphosphonate therapy

❌ DISTRACTOR ANALYSIS

C) Serum calcium concentration	Bisphosphonates can cause transient hypocalcemia, but the fracture is from impaired remodeling, not calcium abnormality.
D) Serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol	Vitamin D levels are not directly affected by bisphosphonates. Not the mechanism of atypical fractures.
E) Serum PTH concentration	PTH may be secondarily elevated if calcium drops, but this is not the primary mechanism of bisphosphonate-related fractures.

sections.title: THE NBME BLUEPRINT & TWO-STEP LOGIC
sections.body:
Target Concept: Respiratory Physiology — Ventilation-Perfusion (V/Q) Relationships

Core Mechanism: A foreign body (candy) has been aspirated into the left mainstem bronchus, obstructing airflow to the left lung. Blood continues to perfuse the left lung (perfusion maintained), but ventilation is blocked → V/Q = 0 in the affected lung (intrapulmonary shunt). The unventilated but perfused lung returns deoxygenated blood to the left atrium, mixing with oxygenated blood from the right lung → decreased O₂ saturation (93%).

Multi-Step Logic:

[Step 1] Choking episode while eating → FOREIGN BODY ASPIRATION

[Step 2] Decreased breath sounds on LEFT → obstruction of LEFT bronchus

[Step 3] Left lung: perfused but NOT ventilated → V/Q = 0 (shunt)

[Step 4] Deoxygenated blood from left lung mixes with

oxygenated blood from right lung

[Step 5] → Decreased systemic O₂ saturation (93%) ✓

[Step 6] This is VENTILATION-PERFUSION MISMATCH ✓

sections.title: VIGNETTE CLUES & PATTERN-RECOGNITION HACKS
sections.body:
Diagnostic Anchors:

🔑 3-year-old + eating candy + sudden coughing/gagging = FOREIGN BODY ASPIRATION

🔑 Decreased breath sounds on LEFT = obstruction of left bronchus

🔑 O₂ sat 93% = hypoxemia (not severe, because right lung is compensating)

🔑 CXR likely shows hyperinflation of left lung (air trapping distal to obstruction) or atelectasis

The "Hack": Any time a question describes hypoxemia and asks for the MECHANISM, think through the 5 causes of hypoxemia:

V/Q mismatch (most common cause overall) ✓

Right-to-left shunt (intracardiac — ASD, VSD, PDA)

Diffusion impairment (thickened alveolar membrane — fibrosis)

Hypoventilation (↑ PCO₂ — neuromuscular, obesity)

Low inspired O₂ (high altitude)

The Reversal: The question specifies "extrapulmonary right-to-left shunt" as a separate choice (Choice C). This is an INTRACARDIAC shunt (e.g., ASD, VSD). The foreign body causes an INTRAPULMONARY problem, not an intracardiac one. This distinction eliminates Choice C.

sections.title: SYSTEMATIC DISTRACTOR EXPOSURE
sections.body:
Choice	Why It's Wrong
A) Decreased chest wall compliance	Decreased chest wall compliance = restrictive chest wall disease (kyphoscoliosis, obesity, ankylosing spondylitis). This 3-year-old has a normal chest wall. The problem is airway obstruction, not chest wall restriction.
B) Diffusion defect	Diffusion impairment occurs with thickened alveolar-capillary membrane (pulmonary fibrosis, asbestosis) or decreased surface area (emphysema). A foreign body does NOT affect the diffusion barrier — it blocks AIRFLOW.
C) Extrapulmonary right-to-left shunt	An extrapulmonary (intracardiac) shunt = blood bypassing the lungs entirely (e.g., through ASD, VSD, PDA with Eisenmenger). This child has no cardiac defect. The problem is INTRAPULMONARY — blood goes to the left lung but that lung isn't ventilated. This is V/Q mismatch (specifically, intrapulmonary shunt where V/Q = 0), NOT an extrapulmonary shunt.
D) Increased chest wall compliance	Increased chest wall compliance is seen in neonates/infants (very compliant chest wall → paradoxical breathing). While a 3-year-old has relatively compliant chest wall, this is NOT the cause of his hypoxemia. The foreign body is.
